paragraphs: Starbridge sells an AI sales intelligence platform to companies whose customers are public-sector buyers. The target user is anyone selling into state and local government, K-12 districts, or higher education.

The platform collects buying signals from public sources such as district and university websites, board and trustee minutes, budget reports, grants, news, job postings, and FOIA requests. A signal, in the company's definition, is an early sign that a district, university, or agency is planning to spend. It claims to scan more than 320,000 public sector entities daily, surfacing budgets, board discussions, and leadership changes. Those signals and enriched accounts push into Salesforce and HubSpot. The platform also centralizes thousands of state, local, education, and university bid portals.

The buyers are go-to-market teams, and the company puts the number at more than 400 selling to government agencies, K-12, and higher education. On data quality, Starbridge cites a recent test of 14,000 emails with a 98% accuracy rate. New accounts are assigned a customer success manager who builds a tailored target list and syncs it into the CRM in the first week.
